problem:
A particle moves with constant acceleration. The velocity of the particle equals $(-4i+9j)\,\text{ft/s}$ both when $t=0\,\text{s}$ and $t=7\,\text{s}.$ What is the acceleration of the particle?

$a=($
{{field-1}}$\,i$
$+$
{{field-2}}$\,j\,)\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}$
worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=-4i+9j,\,v=-4i+9j,\,t=7
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ -4i+9j & =(-4i+9j)+a(7) \\ 0 & =7a \\ a & =(0\,i+0\,j)\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
